1.why: All six screens show a static, clean layout with no moving images, animations, or pop-ups.

2.why: Primary headings and blue action buttons stand out clearly against the white cards and dark header.

3.why: Each step presents a single focused form so the needed field and button are immediately visible.

4.why: The user must remember and re-enter long recovery/security codes across multiple sequential steps with no persistent aids.

5.why: No password-manager hints, autofill attributes, or “remember me” options appear on any screen.

6.why: Aside from the demo pre-filled recovery code, the UI shows no saved or familiar user items to recognize.

7.why: Labels and instructions are short, high-contrast, and written in plain language.

8.why: No error messages or validation feedback are shown in any of the provided screenshots.

9.why: A test recovery code is displayed as an example in step 2, but later fields lack input examples or format hints.

10.why: No alternative authentication choices (password, code, face login, etc.) are offered; only a single code/password path exists.

11.why: Each screen presents exactly one task and at most one primary action, avoiding choice overload.

12.why: Intermediate log messages and the final green ‘Recovery complete’ banner clearly state the outcome of each action.

13.why: Only static ‘Stay safe’ warnings appear; no contextual help or short tips are provided for new steps.

14.why: The linear flow lets a user re-enter a code after a mistake, yet no explicit retry guidance or edit controls are shown.

15.why: Header, card layout, button style and ‘Stay safe’/Logs panels remain identical across all six steps.
